clue.text: Penny's relationship with Bob near to end of engagement produces drama

parts.note: in old British money a bob was a shilling of twelve pennies, so a penny was one twelfth of it
near means nigh, close by

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of engagement is used

explanation.surface: Some romantic tale about a girl and her boyfriend, close to calling off the engagement, makes for theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is old British slang for a shilling, which held twelve pence; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Shakespeare comedy, so a play or piece of drama.

clue.text: Lay down cards taking in bridge opponents capable of defence

indicators.note: taking in tells us the card word wraps around another piece

parts.note: in card games to table cards is to lay them face up
in bridge, East and North are opposing players, E and N

explanation.surface: A bridge player shows their hand, trapping both opponents, and can hold out.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, so any two of N, E, S, W can be opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or defended.

clue.text: Beg favour after people losing head

indicators.note: after tells us the favour word is placed following the other piece
losing head means the first letter of the word for people goes

parts.note: men are people
a treat is a special favour or kindness

explanation.surface: Asking for a favour after people have lost their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or implore, to beg.

clue.text: Middle-aged and single

definitions.meaning: an age in the middle years of a life
a seven-inch single record played at that many revolutions per minute

explanation.definitionFit: The number can describe someone in middle age, and a single record is a disc spun at that rpm.

clue.text: They're full of stingers giving nettle-rash

definitions.meaning: beehives hold bees, insects with stings
an itchy skin rash, also called urticaria

explanation.definitionFit: Beehives are full of stinging bees, and urticaria, or nettle-rash, is also called by that name.

clue.text: Teacher's developed here, to teach

definitions.meaning: Teacher's is a Scotch whisky brand, and whisky is distilled in a still
to implant ideas gradually, to instruct

explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to gradually impress an idea or habit on someone, a way of teaching; whisky also matures in a still.

clue.text: The toad's transformed for lovers' tryst

indicators.note: transformed suggests the letters change into a new arrangement, as a fairytale toad becomes a prince

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A fairytale toad turns into a prince for a romantic meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot date is an exciting romantic engagement, a meeting between lovers.

clue.text: One churning out some prints is artist

definitions.meaning: an impression is a printing run, so one who produces them
a painter of the Monet school

explanation.definitionFit: Monet and Renoir belonged to the school of painting of this name; the word also suggests a maker of printed impressions.

clue.text: One's subtitle alternatively expression of surprise on seeing its author

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
what, you? is a cry of surprise at seeing someone
Will is William Shakespeare, author of the play in 1-across

explanation.surface: A book's subtitle, or an exclamation on meeting the person who wrote it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points to 1-across, whose full title carries this alternative subtitle.
explanation.definitionFit: The play at 1-across has the full title with this second phrase as its alternative subtitle.

clue.text: Great church parson I removed

indicators.note: removed tells us the letter named just before it is taken out of the clergyman word

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman or minister

explanation.surface: A big cathedral-like church has had its vicar ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, often originally a monastery church.

clue.text: Travel document not completed by one corrupt returning traveller

indicators.note: not completed tells us the travel document word loses its last letter

parts.note: a visa is a travel document stamped in a passport
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for corrupt is read backwards

parts.note: to corrupt is to rot

explanation.surface: A traveller whose papers are unfinished is a bent official coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone travelling to a place to stay a while, a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Bremner holding decline back in crime

indicators.note: holding tells us the comedian's first name wraps around another piece

parts.note: Rory Bremner is a British impressionist and comedian

indicators.note: back tells us the word for decline is read backwards

parts.note: to ebb is to decline or recede

explanation.surface: A comedian, clinging to a declining career, slips back into crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory Bremner is a British TV impressionist; 'in' is a link word. 'back' turns EBB into BBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery is theft by force or threat, a crime.

clue.text: In trouble, Popeye's opening his can — of this?

definitions.text: In trouble, Popeye's opening his can — of this?

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are in disarray and must be rearranged
opening means the first letter of the sailor's name is used

explanation.surface: With the cartoon sailor in a fix, he pulls open the tin of his favourite food.
explanation.walkthrough: Popeye the cartoon sailor gains strength by eating tinned spinach, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye's famous strength-giving canned vegetable is the leafy green spinach.

clue.text: Fish gave off a whiff

definitions.meaning: in British spelling, the past tense of smell

explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small food fish, and in British usage the word is also the past tense of smell.

clue.text: Where we may find used paintbrush broke

definitions.text: Where we may find used paintbrush
definitions.meaning: a used brush is put to soak in turps or other solvent, so it is the answer
broke means having no money, bankrupt

explanation.definitionFit: Someone insolvent cannot pay their debts, so is broke; split in two, the word also says a brush is soaking in turps.

clue.text: Function featuring a performance that's gloomy

indicators.note: featuring tells us the function word has other pieces placed inside it

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a turn is a stage act or performance

explanation.surface: A social event with a stage act turns out to be dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means dark and gloomy in temperament, after the planet's supposed influence.

clue.text: I am priggish type, not unwise

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a prude is a priggish, easily shocked person
NT is a short form of not, as in contractions like don't

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a prig but insists they are not foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent is a direct synonym of unwise or rash.

clue.text: Spanish food contains bit of turkey bone

indicators.note: contains tells us the dish wraps around another piece

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: a bit of the bird is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Spanish rice dish has a scrap of turkey bone in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a bone in the leg.

clue.text: Mounted second-rate attack giving abuse

parts.note: mounted means up, as on horseback
B is second-rate, below A grade
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: Cavalry make a feeble charge and get a tongue-lashing.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid is to scold or reproach, to abuse verbally.

clue.text: Some colossal volley

indicators.note: some of tells us the answer is a run of letters within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A huge barrage of gunfire is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both a hidden run across 'colossal volley' and a fair picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a great volley of fire.

clue.text: Get very little writing as pen tip's broken

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A broken nib means only a scrap gets written.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or extract, here of text.

clue.text: New York statue terribly damaged — that's not right

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of the word before it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A New York monument is badly damaged, which is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TERRIBLY, less one R ('that's not right'), are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor, often called just by its last word.

clue.text: Famous aristocrat retaining part-time soldiers

indicators.note: retaining tells us the aristocrat word keeps another piece inside it

parts.note: a noble is an aristocrat
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A celebrated lord keeps a troop of reservists.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means worthy of note, prominent or well known.

clue.text: Antelope dash over Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: dash, meaning flair or verve, is elan
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An antelope sprints across Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Artist visiting Cockney area displaying full range of colours

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
visiting means in, as in staying in a place
Bow is a district in East London, home of Cockneys born within sound of Bow bells

explanation.surface: A painter calls on the East End and shows off every shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, the traditional Cockney heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, rainbow describes something multicoloured, showing the whole spectrum.

clue.text: Oriental princess has last month in hospital with touch of anaemia

indicators.note: in tells us the last-month abbreviation sits inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ult, short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

indicators.note: a touch of something is just a little of it, so the first letter only

explanation.surface: An eastern princess spent the previous month in a clinic being treated for mild anaemia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word. Ult (ultimo) is old letter-writing shorthand for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife, mother or daughter of a sultan, an eastern ruler.

clue.text: Make threat to London College with no short answer

indicators.note: with no tells us the abbreviation for answer is dropped from the college name

parts.note: Imperial College is a university in London
A is a common abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Threatening a university, someone gets no curt reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Imperial College London is a leading science university.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to endanger, to make something under threat.

clue.text: What parachutist should have done with a change of side for rich countryfolk

indicators.note: side here is left or right, so L, an abbreviation for left, swaps for R for right

parts.note: a parachutist ought to have come down softly, landed gently

explanation.surface: Advice for a skydiver is twisted to describe wealthy rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of GENTLY is the one that changes side to R.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed gentry are the old class of wealthy landowners living on country estates.
